subject: Post-demo: SparkBridge integration qualification & prompt governance playbook
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Alyssa Greene <alyssa@sparkbridge.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-11T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Post-demo: SparkBridge integration qualification & prompt governance playbook

Hi Alyssa — thanks again for carving out time today. Solid conversation from our side; quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum.

Summary of today's demo
- Showed a hosted Redwood API proof-of-concept with a sample flow that uses structured tool-calling to retrieve internal KB entries and a reranker for candidate passages.
- Discussed authentication options (API key for dev, mTLS or VPC peering for production Dedicated/Private).
- Walked through embedding-based semantic search + a lightweight reranker for higher-precision retrieval.

Main technical notes / open questions
1) Auth & network: you mentioned a strict VPC-only deployment for prod — can you confirm whether you require customer-managed NAT and whether firewall rules are managed by your infra team?
2) Routing / latency SLOs: target 95th-percentile token latency of <350ms for interactive agents; need to confirm expected qps during peak.
3) Tooling & structured output: you liked tool-calling for actions; we proposed JSON Schema-driven outputs. Do you have existing schema examples for the actions (create-ticket, lookup-customer)?
4) Prompt governance: you asked about versioned system prompts, prompt-injection mitigations, and red teaming cadence — we can propose a lightweight playbook + eval suite.

Attachments I shared: sparkbridge-integration-checklist.xlsx (spreadsheet checklist), sparkbridge-arch-diagram.png (high-level diagram).

Proposed next steps (short timeline)
- Your team: confirm network constraints (VPC/firewall/NAT) and list of prod schemas for tool outputs (by 2027-04-14).
- Our side: send a one-page Integration Playbook draft that outlines SDK setup, auth patterns, routing policies, and prompt governance (by 2027-04-13).
- Schedule a 30–45m technical integration call with your infra and security (suggested slot: Tue 2027-04-15 10:00 PT).

If that aligns, I'll loop in our solutions engineer to draft the playbook and include a short checklist for your procurement team.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0198

Subject: Re: Post-demo: SparkBridge integration qualification & prompt governance playbook

Thanks Jordan — great demo and very helpful recap. Quick answers inline: 

1) Network: For prod we require VPC connectors and prefer not to expose any public endpoints. Our infra team manages firewall rules; we can provide a short list of IP ranges if you need them.
2) Latency / qps: Expected peak for initial rollout is ~30 rps with burst to 90 rps. Targeting sub-400ms p95 is realistic for us.
3) Schemas: We have two canonical action schemas (ticket_create, account_lookup). I'll attach the current JSON Schema for ticket_create in a follow-up.
4) Prompt governance: We're very interested in versioned system prompts and red-team exercises. We currently have informal prompt notes; would appreciate a baseline template for versioning and injection mitigations.

Links: I'm looping our procurement contact (procure@sparkbridge.io) and Tom will coordinate internal security availability.

Can you send the playbook draft by EOD tomorrow? We can review and then set the tech call.

Best,
Alyssa
Head of Product | SparkBridge
alyssa@sparkbridge.io

Date: 2027-04-12T08:37:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: SparkBridge integration qualification & prompt governance playbook

Thanks Alyssa — attaching the Integration Playbook draft and a short example prompt-versioning template. High-level attachments: sparkbridge-integration-checklist.xlsx (updated), Integration-Playbook-v1 (Drive link included below).

Playbook highlights (summary)
- SDK & auth: recommend starting with our hosted API + API key for POC, then Dedicated with VPC peering for Prod. We document token rotation, KMS integration, and optional mTLS.
- Routing: policy-based routing by region and cost tier; fallback to a smaller/quantized model if p95 latency threatens the SLO.
- Structured outputs: we recommend JSON Schema + output validators in the SDK; samples included for ticket_create.
- Embeddings & rerank: hybrid approach — use dense embeddings for recall and a small cross-encoder reranker for final scoring. Recommend offline retraining cadence for the reranker.
- Prompt governance: maintain a prompt registry (versioned entries), require tests/evals on any system-prompt changes, and run quarterly red-team sessions for injection vectors.

Request: can your infra/security share the firewall/IP constraints and a contact for a short network-only call?

Drive: https://drive.company/shared/SparkBridge/Integration-Playbook-v1
HubSpot: https://hubspot.company/contacts/SB-4321

Jordan

I'll take the doc and incorporate these items and then we'll send to Alyssa + Tom and their security contact.
